userStories.title: Audit job dispatch, cancel, requeue and ticket-job unlink
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record each committed job dispatch, cancel, requeue and ticket-job unlink atomically with its write, exposing the internal dispatch auditKey seam for thread handoffs.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

`dispatch` records under `opts.auditKey`, defaulting to `fleet.job.dispatch`. `ThreadsService.plan` passes `thread.plan` and `run` passes `thread.run`, the route keys of `POST …/threads/:id/plan` and `…/run`. The dispatch is the whole write of those routes, so they record one entry, under their own key, and no `fleet.job.dispatch` entry beside it. The type is `auditKey?: 'fleet.job.dispatch' | 'thread.plan' | 'thread.run'`.

`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last. None of `FleetJobsService`, `FleetTicketsService`, `PrismaChatThreadRepository`, `ApprovalsService` or `AssistantActionDecisions` has an `@Optional()` parameter, so audit-core's rule puts it last in each constructor.

`projectId` is the row's project. A job's, a thread's (a workspace thread's home project) and a ticket's project. An approval's entry has the approval's `projectId`, `null` for a global budget policy's ask.

Writer instructions:
- `FleetJobsService.dispatch`: `record` inside, after `activity.record`; key `opts.auditKey ?? 'fleet.job.dispatch'`.
- `FleetJobsService.cancel`: `record` inside each of the three paths that write: the two early server-side `CANCELLED` returns (each records before its `return`) and the runner-command path; not on the already-requested return. Cancel reaches only `QUEUED`, `ASSIGNED`, `RUNNING` and `UPLOADING` (a terminal job is a 409).
- `FleetJobsService.requeue`: `record` inside, after `transitions.apply`: its result is held in a local and returned after `record` (today the callback returns `this.transitions.apply(...)` directly). Requeue reaches only `CRASHED`, `FAILED` and `CANCELLED`.
- `FleetTicketsService.unlink`: `record` inside, after `events.record`.

Summary/resource contract: dispatch (including thread handoffs) uses resourceType `fleet-job`, resourceId created job id, projectId job.projectId, summary `<COMMAND> on repo <repoId>`, then `, thread <threadId>` when the job has a thread and `, schedule <scheduleId>` when it has a schedule. Cancel uses `fleet.job.cancel`, same job resource, summary `cancelled from <STATE>` for server end or `cancel requested in <STATE>` for runner command. Requeue uses `fleet.job.requeue`, same job resource, summary `requeued from <STATE>`. `<STATE>` is the job's state before the write. Unlink uses `fleet.ticket-job.unlink`, resourceType `ticket`, resourceId ticket id, projectId ticket project, summary `job <jobId> unlinked`. Never include feature, ref, title, comments, profiles or spec paths. Audit attribution comes from the existing action context, not activity's USER constants. DuplicateActiveJobError rolls back the transaction and its entry before the existing 409 mapping; recorder rejection propagates and rolls back the job.

Changes: append AuditRecorder to FleetJobsService and FleetTicketsService. Append mockAuditRecorder from common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts to all direct constructors in fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts, fleet-jobs.config-requeue.spec.ts, fleet-jobs.thread-requeue.spec.ts, fleet-jobs.thread-handoff.spec.ts and fleet-tickets.service.spec.ts; the existing assertions are kept. Add test/integration/audit/audit-fleet-jobs.integration.spec.ts using AppModule HTTP and stored rows, plus co-located ordering/default/override unit checks.

**Scope** — In: dispatch/cancel/requeue/unlink recorder calls, internal opts and constructor compatibility. Out: US-004's plan/run callers, US-002/003/004's repository thread actions, US-005/006's approval decisions, US-007's pickup. Recording job placement (`PlacementService.placeJob` after dispatch and requeue) and runner-reported job transitions is out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-ops`). Choosing the key a scheduled fire records under (`fleet.job.dispatch` today, possibly `system.schedule.dispatch`) and the ACs for scheduled dispatch are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-ops`); this feature leaves the ticker's `dispatch` call unchanged.

**Interface** — Existing AuditRecordInput { key: string; resourceType: string; resourceId: string; projectId?: string | null; summary?: string }, AuditRecorder.record(input) and AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf) are read-only. Changed dispatch options: `opts: { scheduleId?; ticketActor?; threadId?; auditKey?: 'fleet.job.dispatch' | 'thread.plan' | 'thread.run' }`. Public route responses, placement and live events are unchanged.

userStories.title: Audit thread create, cap update and archive in both scopes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shared thread audit-key helper and atomically audit thread creation, cap changes and archive for project and workspace threads.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — Thread writes record in `PrismaChatThreadRepository`. Its `create`, `updateCap`, `command`, `archive`, `publish`, `discard` and `sendMessage` each own the write's `txManager.run` (or, for `create`, a single insert). Recording in the services instead would need an outer `audited` around those calls, and that breaks two things. `sendMessage` re-runs its transaction when a send races a new job (`kind: 'retry'`), and inside an outer transaction the retry would re-read inside the same one. `ThreadsService.create` turns the insert's `repo_feature` unique violation into a 409, and a nested run that throws poisons the outer transaction (`PrismaTransactionManager.run`, SEC-16). The repository therefore injects `AuditRecorder`, the same way it already injects `FleetActivityService` for the activity rows it writes in the same transactions. This departs from `.nax/rules/api-data.md`'s layering (a repository owns Prisma access only), as the existing `FleetActivityService`, `PlacementService` and `RunnerNotifier` injections already do; extracting the thread transactions into a service is not this feature's.

The workspace key is chosen by `threadAuditKey(action, workspace)`. A new pure function in `src/fleet/threads/thread-audit.ts`. The repository passes `scope.kind === 'workspace'` (for `create`, `input.kind === 'WORKSPACE'`). `create`, `message` and `archive` have workspace keys (`thread.workspace.create`, `thread.workspace.message.send`, `thread.workspace.archive`). `cap`, `stop`, `end-session` and `answer` use the same key in both scopes, the keys `WorkspaceThreadsService.assertThreadKey` checks. `publish`, `discard`, `plan` and `run` exist only for project threads.

Full helper table (false / true): create → thread.create / thread.workspace.create; message → thread.message.send / thread.workspace.message.send; archive → thread.archive / thread.workspace.archive; cap → thread.cap.update / thread.cap.update; stop → thread.stop / thread.stop; end-session → thread.end-session / thread.end-session; answer → thread.answer / thread.answer; publish → thread.publish / thread.publish; discard → thread.discard / thread.discard. The `workspace` true cells of `publish` and `discard` are defined for completeness and unused: those repository methods take a `projectId` and exclude `WORKSPACE` threads.

`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last. None of `FleetJobsService`, `FleetTicketsService`, `PrismaChatThreadRepository`, `ApprovalsService` or `AssistantActionDecisions` has an `@Optional()` parameter, so audit-core's rule puts it last in each constructor.

Writer instructions: create — wrap the insert in `audit.audited`; updateCap — `record` inside, after the update; archive — `record` inside, after the update; not on the already-archived `null` return. Each entry resourceType is `thread`, resourceId thread id, projectId the thread's own project including a workspace thread's home. Create uses threadAuditKey('create', workspace), summary `created <KIND>` (REPO, PROJECT or WORKSPACE); cap uses thread.cap.update, summary `fields: maxCostUsd`; archive uses threadAuditKey('archive', workspace), summary `archived`. Never include title or any user-entered content. A repo_feature insert conflict rolls back its audit and still maps to 409 threads.featureTaken.

A follow-on write in its own transaction records its own entry. Archiving a thread with a live job cancels the job afterwards (`ThreadsService.archive`, `WorkspaceThreadsService.archive`), and a budget decide that raises and resumes requeues each selected job afterwards (`ApprovalsService.decide`, plan D232). Each of those is a committed write in a separate transaction, so it records `fleet.job.cancel` or `fleet.job.requeue` next to the action's own entry. This differs from audit-core's "record only the action" rule, which covers writes inside one transaction.

Changes: create src/fleet/threads/thread-audit.ts and its co-located spec; inject AuditRecorder into PrismaChatThreadRepository; instrument only create/updateCap/archive here. Append mockAuditRecorder from common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts to every direct constructor in prisma-chat-thread.repository.spec.ts, prisma-chat-thread.discard.spec.ts and thread-scope.spec.ts; the existing assertions are kept. Add test/integration/audit/audit-fleet-threads-lifecycle.integration.spec.ts. Enable and restore FLEET_CFG.threadsEnabled, use binding-based human/agent fixtures, fresh per-AC threads and stored audit rows through fixtureDb(app). A workspace agent's custom global role uses WORKSPACE_AGENT_KEYS, plus thread.create in the home project and an anchor repo.

**Scope** — In: full pure helper mapping, required repository dependency and create/cap/archive audit in both scopes. Out: US-003's command/publish/discard and US-004's sends/handoffs. US-002 only: auditing the `fleet.job.cancel` that `ThreadsService.archive` triggers is not this story's code; US-001's `cancel` records it, and US-002 only asserts it is there.

**Interface** — Verbatim helper declaration:
```typescript
// src/fleet/threads/thread-audit.ts
export type ThreadAuditAction = 'create' | 'message' | 'archive' | 'cap' | 'stop' | 'end-session' | 'answer' | 'publish' | 'discard';

/** The catalog key a thread write records under; a workspace thread's create, message and archive have their own keys. */
export function threadAuditKey(action: ThreadAuditAction, workspace: boolean): string;
```
Use existing read-only AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf) for create and record(input) in the existing transactions. Returned records and route contracts are unchanged.

userStories.title: Audit thread commands, publish and discard
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit stop, end-session, answer, publish and discard inside the repository transactions that commit their commands or jobs.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

The workspace key is chosen by `threadAuditKey(action, workspace)`. A new pure function in `src/fleet/threads/thread-audit.ts`. The repository passes `scope.kind === 'workspace'` (for `create`, `input.kind === 'WORKSPACE'`). `create`, `message` and `archive` have workspace keys (`thread.workspace.create`, `thread.workspace.message.send`, `thread.workspace.archive`). `cap`, `stop`, `end-session` and `answer` use the same key in both scopes, the keys `WorkspaceThreadsService.assertThreadKey` checks. `publish`, `discard`, `plan` and `run` exist only for project threads.

Writer instructions: `PrismaChatThreadRepository.command` — `record` inside, after `createCommand`; action from `type` (`THREAD_STOP_TURN` → `stop`, `THREAD_CLOSE` → `end-session`, `THREAD_ANSWER` → `answer`). `PrismaChatThreadRepository.publish`, `discard` — `record` inside, on each path that wrote a command or a job. Use the US-002 repository dependency and helper; no additional service-level outer transaction.

Summary/resource contract: each entry resourceType `thread`, resourceId thread id and projectId thread.projectId (workspace home project where applicable). Stop/end-session/answer keys are `thread.stop` / `thread.end-session` / `thread.answer` with summary `stop requested` / `end requested` / `answered`. Publish key is `thread.publish`, summary `publish job <jobId>` for a new job or `publish into session <jobId>` for the live-session command. Use the active session's id for the latter even though the public response jobId remains null. Discard key is `thread.discard`, summary `discard job <jobId>`. Only ids and fixed literals enter summaries, never answer text or other request content. A thread command with no live session remains 409 threads.noSession with no entry. Publish without written paths and without an active job remains 409 with no entry.

Do not modify session fences or lock order. Publish/discard exclude WORKSPACE; helper true cells for these actions are defined but unused. A new repository-created THREAD job receives the thread action entry, not a second fleet.job.dispatch entry. Notification and placement remain after commit and all returned values/refusals are unchanged. Add test/integration/audit/audit-fleet-threads-commands.integration.spec.ts; enable/restore FLEET_CFG.threadsEnabled and seed each AC's own thread. For live sessions use protocolVersion 4, capabilities {...FLEET_CAPS, threadWrite:true}, enabled true and fresh lastSeenAt, a thread with runnerId plus a RUNNING THREAD job and SESSION turn; publish into session requires no turn in flight and the session's requester. Use fixtureDb(app), real HTTP and stored AuditEntry queries.

**Scope** — In: command/publish/discard audit calls for their writing branches, including shared workspace command keys. Out: US-002's create/cap/archive/helper construction; US-004's message send and plan/run dispatch keys. No new runner-protocol or placement audit and no session authorization changes.

**Interface** — Consume the existing US-002 declaration verbatim:
```typescript
export type ThreadAuditAction = 'create' | 'message' | 'archive' | 'cap' | 'stop' | 'end-session' | 'answer' | 'publish' | 'discard';

/** The catalog key a thread write records under; a workspace thread's create, message and archive have their own keys. */
export function threadAuditKey(action: ThreadAuditAction, workspace: boolean): string;
```
AuditRecorder.record(input) remains the existing read-only API; repository and REST signatures do not change.

Writer instructions: `PrismaChatThreadRepository.sendMessage` — `record` inside, on the two paths that stored a message; not on the duplicate or the retry return. `ThreadsService.plan`, `run` — pass `{ threadId, auditKey: 'thread.plan' }` / `'thread.run'`.

Summary/resource contract: message send uses threadAuditKey('message', input.scope.kind === 'workspace'), giving `thread.message.send` or `thread.workspace.message.send`, resourceType `thread`, resourceId thread id and projectId thread.projectId including workspace home. New session job summary `message <messageId>, job <jobId>`; live-session input summary `message <messageId>`. Never include input.text, repo context, titles, feature names or delivered outcome notes. A repeated stored clientMessageId makes the repository and ThreadsService.sendMessage return deduplicated:true and records nothing. ThreadsController.sendMessage consumes that internal flag to return HTTP 200 but serializes only { message, jobId }; do not add deduplicated to the public response. For the repeated-POST integration criterion, use a call-through spy on the real ThreadsService.sendMessage and await its recorded result to observe deduplicated:true without stubbing the route, executing a second domain write or changing the HTTP contract. Both pre-lock and post-lock duplicate returns and the retry return remain audit-free. A recorder error aborts the message transaction, including ChatMessage, and propagates as an error. Archived/refused sends record nothing. Plan/run use the dispatched job as resourceType `fleet-job`, resourceId job id, projectId job project; summaries `PLAN on repo <repoId>, thread <threadId>` / `RUN on repo <repoId>, thread <threadId>`. Do not add a service-level record beside dispatch.

In threads.service.spec.ts change the five exact opts expectations (baseline lines 116, 166, 212, 249 and 515; three of them use objectContaining on the dto but still pin the opts exactly) from { threadId:'t1' } to the correct plan or run auditKey plus threadId; the other assertions are kept. Boot AppModule, enable/restore FLEET_CFG.threadsEnabled, use per-AC fixtures and fixtureDb(app) queries. A live-session runner needs protocolVersion 4/threadWrite, enabled and fresh; session must have no turn in flight and be owned by the sender. userStories.title: Audit budget and bash approval decisions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Atomically record budget and bash approval decisions without auditing expiry/job-end closures or changing decision and requeue behavior.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last. None of `FleetJobsService`, `FleetTicketsService`, `PrismaChatThreadRepository`, `ApprovalsService` or `AssistantActionDecisions` has an `@Optional()` parameter, so audit-core's rule puts it last in each constructor.

`projectId` is the row's project. A job's, a thread's (a workspace thread's home project) and a ticket's project. An approval's entry has the approval's `projectId`, `null` for a global budget policy's ask.

Writer instructions: `ApprovalsService.decide` (budget) — `record` inside, after `repo.resolve`, on both decisions. `ApprovalsService.decideBash` — `record` inside, on the `decided` path only.

A follow-on write in its own transaction records its own entry. Archiving a thread with a live job cancels the job afterwards (`ThreadsService.archive`, `WorkspaceThreadsService.archive`), and a budget decide that raises and resumes requeues each selected job afterwards (`ApprovalsService.decide`, plan D232). Each of those is a committed write in a separate transaction, so it records `fleet.job.cancel` or `fleet.job.requeue` next to the action's own entry. This differs from audit-core's "record only the action" rule, which covers writes inside one transaction.

Closes that a decide request commits on the way to a 409 are not recorded here. The bash path closes an ask whose job has ended (`resolvedBy: 'job_ended'`) or expired, and the assistant path expires an action past its `expiresAt`. Both commit and then refuse with 409. They are the same writes `ApprovalExpirySweeper` and `PendingActionExpirySweeper` make, so they belong with those sweepers in audit-fleet-ops (keys `system.approval.expire`, `system.assistant-action.expire`).

Summary/resource contract: budget uses key `fleet.approval.decide.budget`, resourceType `fleet-approval`, resourceId approval id, projectId approval.projectId or null, summary `decision: <decision>` where decision is keep_paused or raise_budget_and_resume. Bash uses `fleet.approval.decide.bash`, same resource contract, summary `decision: <decision>` where decision is allow, allow_for_job or deny. Never copy comment, bash command, amount, feature or other request text into summary. Preserve all existing authorization, no-agent-self-approval, validation and locking gates. Already-decided asks remain 409 and do not add entries; bash ended/epoch-mismatched/expired closes get no decide entry. Budget decision audit is in the first commit, before the independent requeue loop; do not wrap the entire method in audited.

userStories.title: Audit assistant decisions and approved fleet-tool writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record assistant approve/reject commits and prove approved dispatch/requeue/cancel tools inherit the existing assistant action context and approval metadata.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — An approved assistant action records its decide, and its tool records its own writes. `AssistantActionDecisions.approve` and `reject` record `fleet.approval.decide.assistant` inside `settle`'s transaction. The tool then runs outside it (`executeAction`, 2a-D8 step 8) inside `runWithActionContext({ actor: SYSTEM/assistant, onBehalfOf: USER <requester>, origin: 'thread', approval: approvalFor(action) })`. So a `koda_dispatch_job`, `koda_requeue_job` or `koda_cancel_job` the requester approved is recorded by US-001's `dispatch`, `requeue` or `cancel` with that context, including `approverType` `USER`, `approverId` the requester and `approvalRequestId` the action's id. `finalize` (the `EXECUTED`/`FAILED` status and its note) is bookkeeping of the decided action and is audit-integrations' (see Out of Scope).

`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last. None of `FleetJobsService`, `FleetTicketsService`, `PrismaChatThreadRepository`, `ApprovalsService` or `AssistantActionDecisions` has an `@Optional()` parameter, so audit-core's rule puts it last in each constructor.

Closes that a decide request commits on the way to a 409 are not recorded here. The bash path closes an ask whose job has ended (`resolvedBy: 'job_ended'`) or expired, and the assistant path expires an action past its `expiresAt`. Both commit and then refuse with 409. They are the same writes `ApprovalExpirySweeper` and `PendingActionExpirySweeper` make, so they belong with those sweepers in audit-fleet-ops (keys `system.approval.expire`, `system.assistant-action.expire`).

Writer instructions: `AssistantActionDecisions.approve`, `reject` — `record` after `approvals.resolve` and `actions.resolve`. Both run inside settle's existing tx. Entry key `fleet.approval.decide.assistant`, resourceType `fleet-approval`, resourceId approval id, projectId approval.projectId, summary `decision: approve` or `decision: reject`. The human decision is attributed to USER requester/origin rest; the tool's separate job write is SYSTEM/assistant, onBehalfOf USER requester, origin thread, satisfiedBy human and the existing approver fields. Distinguish the decision entry's approval resourceId from the tool entry's approvalRequestId (pending action id). Never include approval comment, preview, tool input, feature or outcome-note text in summaries.

The existing executor already supplies the context; leave executeAction unchanged and do not wrap the decision or tool twice. Preserve creator-only refusal, approval-time permission recheck, expiry status handling and late-bound AssistantActionPort. Only committed decisions audit; repeat, non-requester and expired requests add no decision row. An approved assistant tool that is refused leaves its approval approved and its decide entry committed but records no failed job write. Finalization remains separate bookkeeping.

userStories.title: Audit each successful agent pickup suggestion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Atomically audit each pickup that suggests a ticket alongside its existing agent event and outbox record.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes record none.

**Approach** — Pickup wraps the agent event in `audited`. `suggestTicket` already has `this.audit` (audit-core US-006). It wraps its `recordAgentAction(…, 'TICKET_SUGGESTED', …)` call in `audit.audited`. `KodaDomainWriter.writeAgentAction`'s own `txManager.run` joins it, so the agent event, its outbox row and the entry commit together. The resource is the suggested ticket.

`projectId` is the row's project. A job's, a thread's (a workspace thread's home project) and a ticket's project. An approval's entry has the approval's `projectId`, `null` for a global budget policy's ask.

Use key `agent.pickup`, resourceType `ticket`, resourceId suggested ticket id, projectId project.id, summary `suggested <REF> to <agentSlug>`, where `<REF>` is `<project key>-<number>`. Build the entry for scored[0] only after ranking; leave null return before the audited write when no VERIFIED unassigned ticket exists. The response is unchanged. Preserve suggestTicket's authorization checks: owning agent self-call versus another caller's agent.update key, and the target agent's effective agent.pickup key in the project. Do not change constructors, key handling, ranking, assignment or KodaDomainWriter. Attribution uses existing request action context.

Only committed writes are recorded. A refused request (401, 403, 404, 409, 400) records nothing. So do the writes that find nothing to do: a pickup that finds no verified unassigned ticket (`AgentsService.suggestTicket` returns `null`). Every successful suggesting poll already records an AgentEvent and must record one agent.pickup entry, including repeated suggestions of the same unassigned ticket; no throttling/deduplication is added.

Changes: modify only AgentsService.suggestTicket's recordAgentAction call to use this.audit.audited and add test/integration/audit/audit-fleet-pickup.integration.spec.ts. Use booted AppModule, fixtureDb(app), seedFleetHttpWorld, seedFleetHttpAgent and rosterFleetAgent/role bindings, a real agent API key, a fresh project/ticket per case and AuditEntry queries by resource/key. For the empty case assert the response is null, no TICKET_SUGGESTED event and no pickup entry. Reset existing route throttle counters when needed by setup; never change production throttling.

**Scope** — In: the suggestion's existing event write and its audit wrapper; successful poll multiplicity. Out: US-001's fleet job writers, all thread writers and US-005/006 approval writes. Changing `KodaDomainWriter`, `FleetActivityService`, `TicketEvent`, `AgentEvent`, `FleetJobEvent` or outbox payloads is out of scope; they keep their current shapes. Throttling or de-duplicating pickup entries is out of scope: `GET /agents/:slug/pickup` is polled, and every call that suggests a ticket already writes an `AgentEvent`, so it records one `agent.pickup` entry per suggesting call.

DELIVERY, RISKS AND MIGRATION
Exactly seven implementation stories form one capability/PR. US-001 and US-007 start independently; US-002 depends on US-001, US-003 on US-002, US-004 on US-003; US-005 and US-006 depend on US-001. Serialize edits to the thread repository along that chain. Security-sensitive attribution, existing access gates and session fences justify three-session-tdd isolation. Primary failure risks are recording outside the domain transaction, recording a no-op/duplicate/retry, swallowing an audit-storage error, poisoning a transaction with a handled unique violation, using the post-transition instead of prior state, deriving projectId from a route instead of the row, leaking user content via activity payload reuse, breaking direct constructor tests, duplicating thread-plan dispatch entries, and treating approval.id as tool approvalRequestId. No schema/data migration, backfill, new dependencies, public DTO/controller/status/body/@Requires changes, OpenAPI regeneration or generated CLI changes are needed. Rollout deploys recorder call sites against existing audit-core tables/modules; historic fleet writes remain unaudited. Leave schedule call sites unchanged even though adding dispatch auditing incidentally records current SYSTEM/schedule fires under fleet.job.dispatch; selecting system.schedule.dispatch and scheduled-fire ACs belong to audit-fleet-ops. Failure-table pickup was mistakenly labeled US-001; the binding writer/story inventory and explicit pickup ACs place it in US-007. All table failures are represented in their actual owning stories; only pre-write refusals produce no row here, while expiry/job-end closes may commit without a decide audit as explicitly deferred. The runtime coverage guard/walker, operational writers and assistant finalization are later features, not prerequisites to implement here.
outOfScope: Budgets, schedules, runners and enrollment, repos and repo config (`config-edits`, `drift-checks`), ingest, knowledge, analytics, the runner routes (`/fleet/runner/sync`, `enroll`, logs, bundle upload, tool calls), the test hooks and every fleet system writer are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-ops`).

Choosing the key a scheduled fire records under (`fleet.job.dispatch` today, possibly `system.schedule.dispatch`) and the ACs for scheduled dispatch are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-ops`); this feature leaves the ticker's `dispatch` call unchanged.

Recording job placement (`PlacementService.placeJob` after dispatch and requeue) and runner-reported job transitions is out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-ops`).

The runtime coverage guard and the walker test over write surfaces are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-integrations`).
Changing `KodaDomainWriter`, `FleetActivityService`, `TicketEvent`, `AgentEvent`, `FleetJobEvent` or outbox payloads is out of scope; they keep their current shapes.
Recording refused or failed attempts (403, 409, validation errors) is out of scope; only committed writes are recorded, and refusal records belong to P3's approval engine.

Putting any request value (thread title, message text, answer text, feature name, approval comment, spec path, profile names) into an audit summary is out of scope; summaries carry only the ids, refs, slugs, commands, states and decisions in the contract table.
